title: All Kinds of Form Controls 🎛️
description: Explore text fields, checkboxes, radios, selects, textareas, and more.

slides.title: Text Inputs in Depth ⌨️
slides.content:
# More Than Just `type="text"`

- `email` – browser validates the format, shows an appropriate keyboard on mobile.
- `number` – accepts only numbers; `min`, `max`, `step` attributes fine‑tune it.
- `tel` – telephone number; no strict validation, but shows a phone keypad.
- `url` – expects a full URL.
- `search` – often styled differently, has a clear button.

```html
<input type="number" min="0" max="100" step="5" value="25">
```

quizData.question: Which input type automatically validates for a properly formatted email?
quizData.explanation: `type="email"` triggers browser validation for an email pattern.

slides.title: Checkboxes & Radio Buttons ☑️🔘
slides.content:
# Multiple Choices

- **Checkbox** (`type="checkbox"`) – allows multiple selections. Use the same `name` for a group but it's not required.
- **Radio** (`type="radio"`) – only one selection per group. All radios in a group must share the **same** `name`.

```html
<input type="checkbox" id="agree" name="agree" value="yes">
<label for="agree">I agree</label>

<input type="radio" id="red" name="colour" value="red">
<label for="red">Red</label>
<input type="radio" id="blue" name="colour" value="blue">
<label for="blue">Blue</label>
```
The `value` attribute is what gets sent to the server when selected.

slides.title: Dropdowns with `<select>` and `<option>` 📜
slides.content:
# A Compact List of Options

```html
<label for="country">Country:</label>
<select id="country" name="country">
  <option value="us">United States</option>
  <option value="ca">Canada</option>
  <option value="uk">United Kingdom</option>
</select>
```
- Add `multiple` attribute to allow selecting several options (Ctrl+click).
- `<optgroup>` can group options under labels.

slides.title: Multi‑line Text with `<textarea>` 📄
slides.content:
# For Longer Messages

Unlike `<input>`, `<textarea>` has a closing tag and can hold paragraphs.

```html
<label for="message">Your message:</label>
<textarea id="message" name="message" rows="5" cols="30">Default text</textarea>
```
- `rows` and `cols` set the initial size, but users can resize.
- Use CSS `resize` to control that behaviour.

quizData.question: Which element creates a dropdown list?
quizData.explanation: The `<select>` element, populated with `<option>` children, creates a dropdown.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Pre‑select an Option

Add the `selected` attribute to an `<option>` to make it the default. For checkboxes/radios, use `checked`.
